title: The Bellows Intercept
description: Exactly one striking 16:10 landscape desktop wallpaper, preferably 2560x1600, set inside a historically grounded medieval siege-engine workshop at night beneath an open timber shed beside a walled European town. Massive timber beams, rope coils, oak wheels, iron fittings, stacked counterweights, tool racks, charcoal braziers, and a half-built trebuchet are rendered with practical historical accuracy. In the lower-right, Space Ghost is unmistakable in his muscular white costume, black hood and mask, yellow cape, and red power bands, solemnly working an enormous hand bellows with one gloved hand while holding a tiny surveyor's plumb line in the other, as though certifying the machine's engineering. His cape is pinned safely away from the coals. Tired craftsmen continue their dignified work around him with restrained bewilderment; a patient draft horse watches from shadow. The humor comes only from his misplaced technical confidence and impossible scale. Keep the broad upper sky and roofline dark, sparse, and quiet for a desktop panel, with a calm widget-friendly shadow on the left. No sacred figures, worship, halos, devotional objects, text, lettering, logos, interface elements, watermark, or frame.
prompt:
Create exactly one striking 16:10 landscape desktop wallpaper, preferably 2560x1600, containing a Space Ghost cameo. Space Ghost is the recognizable animated superhero: muscular white costume, black hood and mask, yellow cape, red power bands. The humour is affectionate and understated; he is an out-of-place visitor who takes the occasion completely seriously. Make the visual joke readable without any explanatory text.

The viewer is a devout Christian who loves history, chivalry and the medieval Crusades. Christian subjects, wherever they appear, are depicted straight, reverently and accurately, and are never the butt of the joke. Strict limits, which override anything else in this request: never depict Space Ghost or his companions as Christ, God, the Holy Spirit, an angel, a saint, the Virgin Mary or any holy person; never give them a halo, nimbus, aureole, or any devotional attribute; never place them as the object of veneration, prayer or worship; never show them as clergy performing a sacrament or blessing. Never parody scripture, the crucifixion, the Mass, the Eucharist, baptism, prayer or any act of worship. Altars, crucifixes, icons, relics and the consecrated elements are never props or punchlines. Where a church, monastery, cathedral or sacred art appears, render it with genuine reverence and let the humour come only from Space Ghost being somewhere he plainly does not belong, behaving respectfully.

Follow the supplied medium and treatment exactly and do not default to oil painting unless the request asks for one. Preserve a spacious, quieter upper edge for a desktop panel and leave at least one calm region for desktop widgets. If a theme is supplied, follow its palette throughout; otherwise choose colours that suit the subject naturally. No user interface, words, lettering, logos, watermarks or picture frames. Deliver the actual raster image using built-in native image generation; do not substitute code, SVG or a text description.

Using popular depictions, place spaceghost in those exact poses so they're fully recognizable. Do not blaspheme Christ, spaceghost's visage isn't to be worshipped in any of these images. Spaceghost always worships Christ and never allows himself to be worshipped.

Theme: The Bellows Intercept. A layered fresco-secco and powdered graphite illustration on warm lime plaster, combining matte mineral pigment, hairline architectural drafting, rubbed charcoal haze, and occasional translucent shellac glints on metal. The mood is chivalric, industrial, nocturnal, and gently absurd: a historically grounded medieval siege workshop treated with complete seriousness while an unmistakable cosmic visitor performs the wrong job with heroic concentration. Use a rare palette of furnace-black, bruised blue, chalked apricot, tarnished green-bronze, bone white, and tiny sparks of arterial red. Build broad smoky negative space across the quiet upper edge and leave a calm dark region near the left side for widgets; concentrate tactile detail in the lower-right machinery and figures. No lettering, logos, borders, frames, UI, watermarks, sacred parody, or devotional attributes.
